Definition: to scan, i.e. look intently at; by implication, to regard with pleasure, favor or care
BiblicalUsage: Nabat means to look intently, to scan or regard with care, and it is used for God looking down and for men looking up. In Genesis 15:5 the Lord tells Abram to look toward heaven and count the stars, and in Exodus 3:6 Moses hides his face because he is afraid to look upon God. In Psalm 33:13 the Lord looketh from heaven and beholds all the sons of men, and in Isaiah 5:12 the people regard not the work of the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe looking is never neutral in Scripture, because what we look at shapes what we become. Abram looked at the stars and believed a promise, Moses feared to look at God and was sent, and the Lord looks at all of us and sees truly. I hold that I want my looking to be the kind that notices the work of the Lord.
